claim_boundary: FRED identifies WRESBAL as weekly-average reserve balances held by depository institutions at Federal Reserve Banks. The Federal Reserve explains these are funds institutions hold on deposit at the Fed. These sources establish balance-sheet identity and publication timing, but they do not establish that a four-week increase improves tradable crypto liquidity, predicts BTC returns or supports a profitable long-or-cash policy.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_walcl: WALCL is total Federal Reserve assets; WRESBAL is a specific liability held by depository institutions. Asset growth can be offset by TGA, ON RRP, currency or other liabilities, so the measures are not identical.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_tga_and_on_rrp: TGA and ON RRP measure cash held by Treasury or eligible money-market counterparties; WRESBAL measures bank reserve deposits directly.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_rescue: Do not combine WRESBAL with WALCL, TGA, ON RRP, M2, rates, Treasury issuance or BTC price after source or outcome access. Do not change the four-week lag, strict growth direction or Friday availability.

adversarial_prior: Higher reserve balances do not prove that banks expand credit or that funds reach crypto markets.
Reserve demand, regulation, payment flows and the ample-reserves operating framework can weaken any risk-asset interpretation.
COVID-era balance-sheet expansion may dominate the historical result and fail annual or regime breadth.
The liability is jointly affected by Fed assets, Treasury deposits, currency, ON RRP and other balance-sheet items; a univariate relation may be confounded.
FRED data are subject to revision; the downloaded history will be a present-vintage source without original weekly vintages.
